title: Lee Larkin's home and the Keppard rehearsals
summary: Howard says Lee Larkin was a non-musician friend of musicians whose place at Washington and Central hosted the rehearsals.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: It mentions here that Lee Larkin's
"The rehearsals of the Keppard band were at Lee Larkin's home."
Yeah, Lee Larkin's. He had got a place down there. Don't you remember Lee Larkin's place down there on Central Avenue?
No, you wouldn't. You was too young.
Was that near Washington and Central?
Yeah, near Washington. Right at Washington and Central.
Who was Lee Larkin? He was a musician?
Oh--he was a friend of musicians?
Just a friend of musicians. Just a guy that always stuck his finger out, and always had his hand out for sump'n.
He didn't have a club or anything, did he?
